residents.personaFr: Gregory Lacharme, un quadragénaire réfléchi qui mêle lecture de philosophie, sorties jazz et balades à vélo, possède toutefois la tendance à ruminer ses décisions et à reporter ses étirements, ce qui se traduit par des douleurs dorsales récurrentes.
residents.personaEn: Gregory Lacharme, a reflective quadragenarian who mixes philosophy reading, jazz outings, and bike rides, tends to overthink decisions and postpone stretching, leading to recurring back pain.

residents.name: Abdelmadjid Chabbi
residents.personaFr: Abdelmadjid Chabbi est un homme réfléchi et prudent, qui trouve sérénité dans la pêche et la marche le long de la Seine, tout en cultivant une légère méfiance envers les nouveautés et une habitude de vérifier deux fois chaque boulon avant de serrer.
residents.personaEn: Abdelmadjid Chabbi finds serenity in fishing and Seine walks, is cautious about new things, and habitually double‑checks each bolt before tightening.

residents.name: Benjamin Dessertenne
residents.personaFr: Benjamin Dessertenne, curieux et légèrement désordonné, passe ses après‑midi à dessiner sur sa tablette tout en laissant tourner ses playlists découvertes, accumule des stickers de street‑art sur son sac à dos et remet parfois à plus tard la saisie de ses dépenses dans son tableau budgétaire.
residents.personaEn: Benjamin Dessertenne, curious and slightly disorganized, spends afternoons drawing on his tablet, curates playlists, sticks street‑art stickers on his backpack, and sometimes delays entering expenses in his budget sheet.

residents.name: Albertine Lacaze
residents.personaFr: Albertine Lacaze allie une spontanéité chaleureuse à une tendance à remettre au lendemain les tâches administratives, tout en cultivant un goût prononcé pour les échanges humains et les petites rituels du quotidien.
residents.personaEn: Albertine Lacaze combines warm spontaneity with a habit of postponing administrative tasks, while cherishing human exchanges and daily rituals.

residents.name: Nina Brunet
residents.personaFr: Nina Brunet, technicienne en médiation sociale qui mêle yoga au bord de la Seine, crêpes bretonnes et tartes flambées, trouve son équilibre entre rigueur budgétaire et élans de compassion, tout en gardant la manie de fredonner Barbara lorsqu’elle vérifie ses tableaux.
residents.personaEn: Nina Brunet, a social‑mediation technician, blends riverside yoga, Breton crêpes, flambeed tarts, strict budgeting, and compassion, often humming Barbara while reviewing her spreadsheets.

residents.name: Florian Ridard
residents.personaFr: Florian Ridard mêle une discrète fascination pour l'art contemporain et le bricolage électronique a une routine de travail méthodique, tout en cultivant une préférence marquée pour la solitude, des moments d'anxiete silencieuse et une tendance a remettre les soins médicaux au lendemain.
residents.personaEn: Florian Ridard mixes a quiet fascination for contemporary art and electronic tinkering with a meticulous work routine, prefers solitude, experiences silent anxiety, and tends to delay medical care.

groups.label: Young renters (18-34)
groups.description: Aged 18-34 and renting (private or social). Tenure is imputed from INSEE census shares.

groups.label: Families with children
groups.description: Household type 'Couple avec enfant(s)' or 'Famille monoparentale' (from the dataset).

groups.label: Students (18-25)
groups.description: Aged 18-25 with occupation 'Autres sans activité professionnelle' (dataset); treated as students.

groups.label: Managers & professionals
groups.description: PCS 'Cadres et professions intellectuelles supérieures' (dataset, re-weighted to INSEE).

groups.label: Households without a car
groups.description: No car in the household (imputed, calibrated to INSEE share of households with a car).

groups.label: Heavy-car owners
groups.description: Household has a car above the Paris heavy-car threshold (thermal/hybrid >= 1.6 t, EV >= 2 t). Imputed with an assumed share of cars.

groups.label: Social-housing tenants
groups.description: Lives in social housing (HLM) — imputed, calibrated to INSEE census share per district.

groups.label: Residents who cannot vote locally
groups.description: Non-EU foreign nationals (imputed from INSEE foreign share and an assumed EU share). They cannot vote in Paris votations.

groups.label: Inner-suburb residents
groups.description: Lives in Hauts-de-Seine, Seine-Saint-Denis or Val-de-Marne (outside the city of Paris).

method.sampling: 1400 residents in Paris allocated to the 20 arrondissements in proportion to INSEE 2022 adults (18+, min 10 each); 600 in the communes of Hauts-de-Seine, Seine-Saint-Denis and Val-de-Marne that intersect the map, in proportion to adults x share of the commune area inside the map, with the communes around the hypothetical data-centre site oversampled (La Courneuve x7, Le Bourget x5, Drancy x3.5, Dugny x3, other neighbours x2.5). Within each district, NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas-France rows are raked to INSEE marginals and drawn without replacement with probability proportional to their raking weight. Half of the dataset's Paris rows have no arrondissement: those are assigned one jointly with their occupation, age band and education (P(arr|occ,age,edu) ∝ P(arr)·P(occ|arr)·P(age|arr)·P(edu|arr), INSEE shares), never uniformly at random. Draws are systematic PPS after sorting by occupation/sex/age/education, with a 20x lower starting weight for rows whose own text names a different arrondissement (keeps texts consistent). Homes: building tiles inside the district, spread out; work: tile in the work district near the job hub. Map: web/public/data/map.json.
method.raking: Iterative proportional fitting per district on sex x occupation (8 PCS groups, 18+), sex x age band (5) and education (7 levels) from the INSEE 2022 census; rows are then drawn by systematic PPS. After sampling, a residual raking weight per departement (sex x occupation, sex x age; capped 0.33-3) corrects what the draw left. `weight` = design weight (district adults / residents drawn, undoing the unequal sampling rates between Paris, suburbs and the boosted communes) x residual raking weight, normalised to mean 1. Use `weight` for every aggregate.
imputation: IMPUTED nationality (french / eu / non_eu): per district, the INSEE 2022 share of foreign nationals is matched exactly; who is foreign depends only on age band, occupation and education (never on names or cultural background). EU share of foreigners is an assumption: {'75': 0.3, '92': 0.3, '93': 0.15, '94': 0.25}.

IMPUTED tenure (owner / private_renter / social_renter): per district, INSEE 2022 shares of people living in owner-occupied, privately rented and HLM dwellings are matched exactly; owners are more likely older, couples, cadres/artisans/retirees.
IMPUTED car (household has >= 1 car): per district, INSEE 2022 share of households with a car is matched exactly; more likely for families, owners, artisans; less likely for students and under-30s.

IMPUTED heavyCar (Paris SUV-fee definition: thermal/hybrid >= 1.6 t or EV >= 2 t): ASSUMPTION 30 % of household cars (no official estimate found), more likely for cadres, artisans, families with children and suburb residents.

IMPUTED registration: EU nationals 25 % registered (assumption); French nationals in Paris registered so that eligible adults match the ~1,375,000 registered voters of the 2023/2024 votations (younger people less often registered); suburbs 88 % of French adults. eligibleParis = lives in Paris AND registered (French or EU).

IMPUTED workplace: retirees and non-working adults have none; 65 % of 18-25 students get a university (Sorbonne/Jussieu, Paris Rive Gauche, Assas, Paris 8 Saint-Denis, Nanterre, Créteil, Condorcet). Workers: own district with probability INSEE 'works in commune of residence' (suburbs) or 40 % (Paris arrondissements, assumption), Paris residents keep the INSEE share working inside Paris; otherwise job hubs by occupation (8e/9e/1er-2e, La Défense, 13e, 15e, 12e, Issy/Boulogne, Saint-Denis Pleyel, Gennevilliers port, Ivry/Vitry, Créteil...) plus a population-proportional spread, with distance decay.

IMPUTED commuteMode: a prior from distance, car and Paris/suburb geography, calibrated per home district to INSEE 2022 mode shares of employed residents (walk, bike, car, public transport; motorised two-wheelers and 'no transport' excluded), then public transport split into metro / RER / bus by geography.

participationBase (not imputed from the LLM): turnout by 5-year age group in the 2022 legislative elections (Insee Première 1928) x diploma ratio of systematic voting (Insee Première 1929) x tenure factor (owner 1.10, private renter 0.95, social renter 0.90 — assumption); 0 for non-EU foreign nationals, who cannot vote. The scenario engine rescales to real turnout.
knownDatasetIssues: Paris (like Lyon and Marseille) is sampled twice: once as the city ('Paris', no arrondissement) and once as its 20 arrondissements — 29.2 rows per 1,000 inhabitants vs ~13 in 92/93/94. Harmless here because we sample fixed quotas per district and rake to INSEE.
49.9% of the dataset's Paris rows (30,693 of 61,456) have commune 'Paris' without an arrondissement; we assigned one jointly with occupation, age and education (districtSource = 'imputed').

Occupation is not conditioned below the departement: Paris rows have 9.7% cadres (INSEE Paris 18+: ~31 %) and 0.7% farmers; similar ~10 % cadres in every departement and arrondissement. Corrected by raking.
No income, tenure, car, commute, workplace or nationality fields: all of these are imputed from INSEE statistics and labelled as such.
Rows that only say 'Paris' still name an arrondissement in their text 47% of the time, invented by the generator (47% of those mentions are the 12e); we never use them as evidence.
Names: a few persona texts start with civil-status artifacts ('Epse Cavuoto ...') or with adjectives instead of the name; we take the name confirmed by the other text fields.
